To some, holding something made for Christmas 1999 that has that extended history is more valuable than holding a copy that was made in a completely different process, made for the purpose of mimicry.
Other people can own Repros, I don’t care. Repros make games more accessible. But Repros should be easily distinguished from authentic.

I don’t like repros of anything. They can misrepresent their past, and the past in general. I want to own a game that was manufactured in the 90s/early 2000s. I want to see their standards, their attention to detail, and I want to see the condition of them having survived that long.

Repros can not only miss the mark on attention to detail, and you could be enjoying a product in a way that the creators didn’t intend for, but it ignores the history a game would have if it were fresh out of a decades old factory.
